text.arabic_uthmani: قَالَتْ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِى لُمْتُنَّنِى فِيهِ ۖ وَلَقَدْ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفْسِهِۦ فَٱسْتَعْصَمَ ۖ وَلَئِن لَّمْ يَفْعَلْ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسْجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونًۭا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ

words.gloss_range: direct feminine singular speech launch governing the full quoted confrontation
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, declaration, and reported judgment; locally narrowed to the wife’s direct quoted declaration.
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَتْ}} ({{tr:qālat}}) opens the ayah as the wife’s completed speech turn, with feminine singular morphology naming her without an explicit noun. The quoted frame holds display, confession, and threat together as one public performance; the same speech-root chain also links this coercive speech to Joseph’s answer in 12:33 and the later confession scene in 12:51.

topics.headline: feminine pro-drop speech launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speaker encoded in the verb before any explicit naming, so the wife seizes the floor at once.
topics.reason: The perfect 3fs speech verb opens and governs the direct quotation.

topics.headline: speech as public declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the saying verb as the channel through which admission, accusation, and coercion become public.
topics.reason: The q-w-l field supports saying and declaring, while local syntax makes the utterance perform several speech acts.

topics.headline: single frame for escalating speech acts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows one speech frame moving from demonstration to confession to threat rather than separate narrator summaries.
topics.reason: The quoted complement extends across the ayah and structures its escalation.

topics.headline: speech-chain echoes across the episode
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this turn answered and re-evaluated by later q-w-l scenes (12:33, 12:51).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give same-surah speech-frame links, especially 12:33 and 12:51.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector binding the opening pointer to the previous scene
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the demonstrative that follows feel like a consequence of what the women just witnessed in 12:31. The particle lets the prior scene function as evidence: so, that is the one you blamed me about.

topics.headline: consequential opening particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wife begins from the previous scene as proof, not from a neutral new topic.
topics.reason: The prefixed particle attaches consequence and sequence to the demonstrative opening.

words.gloss_range: masculine singular demonstrative with feminine plural addressee suffix, pointing Joseph out to the women
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكُنَّ}} ({{tr:dhālikunna}}) points at Joseph while addressing the women through its suffix. The form splits referent and audience in one word: masculine singular for the displayed man, feminine plural for the confronted group, so the grammar itself stages him as exhibit and them as addressees.

topics.headline: referent and audience split in one demonstrative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Joseph and the women separated inside the word’s agreement and suffix structure.
topics.reason: The masculine demonstrative and feminine plural suffix identify different participants.

topics.headline: demonstrative exhibit rather than bare reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the pointing word as a public display, not just a pronoun-like reference.
topics.reason: The far demonstrative operates as staged showing in this scene.

topics.headline: pointer before explanation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Joseph is displayed before the blame clause explains why he matters.
topics.reason: The demonstrative precedes the relative identifier and freezes the topic.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine relative pronoun turning the pointer into an identifying blame clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِى}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) turns the pointer into identification: Joseph is the one around whom the women’s blame was organized. Its masculine singular agreement keeps the clause attached to him, while the following blame relation supplies the wife’s argument.

topics.headline: masculine relative concord fixes referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the relative clause defines Joseph, not the women being addressed.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun agrees with the masculine demonstrative and introduces the modifying clause.

topics.headline: display becomes accusation-bearing identification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the wife convert a visible person into the explanation for the earlier blame.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun hinges the demonstrative to the blame clause.

words.gloss_range: direct public reproach: you women blamed me, with plural accusers and singular object compressed into one verb
words.root_gloss_range: blame, reproach, censure, and finding fault; locally selected as public moral blame aimed at the speaker.
words.prose: {{ar:لُمْتُنَّنِي}} ({{tr:lumtunnanī}}) compresses the confrontation into one blame verb: the women as plural agents, the wife as the explicit object, and the concern completed by the following phrase. The selected sense is reproach and censure, not neutral criticism, and its rarity makes the social blame stand out before the speech pivots to confession and threat. Its dense nūn sequence audibly tightens the personal rebuke, while the blame scene answers the women’s gossip in 12:30 and points toward later reassessment in 12:51.

topics.headline: plural accusers and singular target compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the accusation as a direct you-all-against-me confrontation inside one verbal form.
topics.reason: The 2fp verb with 1sg object suffix and emphatic density encodes the social confrontation.

topics.headline: blame as moral censure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening relation as public reproach, not mild criticism or neutral accountability.
topics.reason: The l-m-m evidence supports blame, upbraiding, and finding fault as the selected sense.

topics.headline: first step in escalation arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees blame become the first move before confession, resistance, command, and threat.
topics.reason: The blame verb sits inside the identifying relative clause and launches the escalation.

topics.headline: blame scenes and selfhood links
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the blame word tied to gossip and later reassessment scenes (12:30, 12:51).
topics.reason: The rows link this blame to the women’s gossip in 12:30 and later truth-telling in 12:51.

topics.headline: tightened blame sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the dense nūn sequence making the reproach sharp and personal.
topics.reason: The phonetic row notes audible tightening in the word.

topics.headline: rare perfect blame form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is not routine vocabulary but a marked blame form in the scene.
topics.reason: The rarity rows mark the perfect l-m-m occurrence as locally salient.

words.gloss_range: preposition-plus-pronoun marking Joseph as the concern or cause of the blame while keeping him unnamed
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِ}} ({{tr:fīhi}}) closes the blame clause by making Joseph the concern around which reproach turns, while still leaving him in pronoun form. The containment or concern sense is selected here, and its contrast with the later separation preposition helps distinguish blame about him from seduction away from his self.

topics.headline: attached pronoun keeps Joseph present but unnamed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Joseph carried as a pronoun, not reintroduced as a named figure.
topics.reason: The suffix refers back to the displayed masculine singular referent.

topics.headline: concern-topic preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the blame located around Joseph as its topic or cause.
topics.reason: The local relation selects concern-about rather than free spatial containment.

topics.headline: tail sealing the blame clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the relative blame clause close before the confession begins.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase completes the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new sworn confession unit
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the speech into a new unit rather than merely adding another item. It separates the first accusation beat from the sworn confession that follows, so the wife’s rhetoric advances in stages.

topics.headline: resumptive opening of confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a fresh confession unit after the blame clause, not a flat continuation.
topics.reason: The conjunction starts the coordinated assertion introduced by the oath-certainty cluster.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lam forming the first part of the sworn-certainty confession
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) begins the oath-colored assertion before the certainty particle. The wife does not merely concede; she certifies the confession against resistant listeners.

topics.headline: lam of sworn emphasis before confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the confession strengthened before the seduction verb arrives.
topics.reason: The lam scopes over the following certainty particle and perfect verb as an emphatic unit.

words.gloss_range: certainty particle locking the following perfect verb as realized past fact
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) joins the preceding lam to make the confession a certified past fact. Before the adversative resistance appears, the seduction attempt is grammatically locked as something she truly did.

topics.headline: certified past confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the seduction claim is not tentative; it is presented as realized and asserted.
topics.reason: With a perfect verb, qad marks realized past fact and participates in the laqad assertion stack.

words.gloss_range: Form III seduction attempt: persistent coaxing directed at Joseph and completed by a separation-from-self complement
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, coaxing, and persistent pursuit; locally selected as a Form III seduction attempt with separation-from-self force.
words.prose: {{ar:رَاوَدتُّهُ}} ({{tr:rāwadtuhū}}) makes the wife the first-person agent and Joseph the attached object of a completed seduction attempt. Form III gives the act persistence and back-and-forth pressure, while the complement that follows narrows the seeking into an attempt to draw him away from his own self; the smoother rolling sound of the verb contrasts with the blocked texture of resistance. Later scenes return to the same seduction-root admission and accusation pattern (12:23, 12:26, 12:51).

topics.headline: Form III first-person seduction verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the wife name herself as the agent of a sustained attempt, not as a passive sufferer of desire.
topics.reason: The perfect Form III 1sg verb with object suffix encodes her agency and Joseph as the acted-upon object.

topics.headline: coaxing and pursuit rather than simple wanting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears seduction as persistent pursuit that tries to move Joseph away from himself.
topics.reason: The r-w-d field and the local complement support coaxing, seeking, and enticement in this frame.

topics.headline: confession sets up resistance pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the sworn confession immediately prepare the contrast with Joseph’s resistance.
topics.reason: The perfect seduction clause is followed by an adversative fa and the resistance verb.

topics.headline: seduction-root recurrence in Joseph scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the same seduction root across accusation, admission, and later truth-telling (12:23, 12:26, 12:51).
topics.reason: The rows name same-surah recurrences of r-w-d and its later interrogation scene.

topics.headline: rolling sound against blocked resistance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the smoother pressure of the seduction verb before the more closed resistance word.
topics.reason: The phonetic row contrasts the texture of the seduction and resistance verbs.

words.gloss_range: separation preposition directing the seduction away from Joseph’s self
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) redirects the seduction from Joseph as a mere object to separation from his self. The preposition is the hinge that makes the attempt an assault on integrity, not only an approach toward a person, and its nasal sound binds directly into the following self phrase.

topics.headline: prepositional hinge before selfhood noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the seduction aiming away-from a protected domain rather than simply toward Joseph.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following self noun as the complement of the seduction verb.

topics.headline: separation sense selected locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees separation-from-self as the controlling relation in the phrase.
topics.reason: The local construction selects separation more strongly than a generic concerning sense.

topics.headline: nasal hinge into self phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the preposition bind into the self phrase it governs.
topics.reason: The phonetic row notes the nasal link into the following noun.

words.gloss_range: Joseph’s own self as the genitive domain targeted by seduction and protected by resistance
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, personhood, desire, and living interiority; locally the protected domain Joseph is enticed away from.
words.prose: {{ar:نَفْسِهِ}} ({{tr:nafsihi}}) names the domain from which Joseph is being enticed away: his own self, marked by the possessive suffix. The root’s breath, desire, and interiority range gives the self a living depth, while local grammar selects bounded selfhood rather than reducing the phrase to desire alone. This targeted self prepares the following self-protection pivot, and the nasal cluster audibly binds the separation phrase to the self noun; later self-language in the surah reopens this inner crisis (12:53, 12:77).

topics.headline: possessive genitive self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the threatened domain as specifically Joseph’s own self, not an abstract selfhood in general.
topics.reason: The genitive noun is governed by the separation preposition and carries Joseph’s suffix.

topics.headline: living selfhood with desire pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels nafs as a living interior domain under pressure, while the local construction keeps selfhood as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The n-f-s range includes self, soul, breath, and desire; the local phrase selects Joseph’s self as the object of attempted separation.

topics.headline: seduction complement matched by resistance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the targeted self prepare for the following self-protection pivot.
topics.reason: The phrase completes the seduction complement before the adversative resistance verb.

topics.headline: nafs thread through Joseph’s inner crises
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this protected self to later self-language in the same story (12:53, 12:77).
topics.reason: The rows cite later n-f-s scenes and the repeated formula around seduction and confession.

topics.headline: nasal binding of separation and self
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase bind the separation preposition to the self noun.
topics.reason: The sound row marks the nasal cluster across the phrase.

words.gloss_range: adversative consequential connector turning seduction pressure into counter-resistance
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the pivot from her completed attempt to Joseph’s counter-move. It carries sequence and contrast at once: therefore, in response to that pressure, he resisted.

topics.headline: adversative pivot after seduction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the resistance as an immediate counter-consequence, not a disconnected next event.
topics.reason: The particle attaches the reversal to the resistance verb and links it to the preceding seduction clause.

words.gloss_range: Form X self-seeking protection and restraint, the central resistance pivot of the ayah
words.root_gloss_range: protection, restraint, preservation, and holding back; locally a Form X self-seeking protection/resistance act.
words.prose: {{ar:اسْتَعْصَمَ}} ({{tr:istaʿṣama}}) is the ayah’s central counter-verb: Joseph actively seeks or causes protection for himself after the seduction attempt. The protection root gives resistance moral preservation and restraint, while Form X keeps the action self-directed in this local frame; its heavy consonant closure and rare perfect form make the pivot feel firm and marked. Corpus echoes of protection with God sharpen the register without replacing the local grammar (3:101, 5:67, 11:43).

topics.headline: Form X self-directed protection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices resistance as active self-protection, not merely refusal or passivity.
topics.reason: The Form X perfect encodes Joseph as the pro-drop subject and selects self-seeking protection.

topics.headline: protection root as moral restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the resistance as preservation of integrity, while the local verb remains a human self-protective act.
topics.reason: The ʿ-ṣ-m range supports protection and restraint; local Form X narrows it to Joseph’s resistance.

topics.headline: central adversative pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the whole ayah turn on this verb between confession and threat.
topics.reason: The verb follows adversative fa and precedes the conditional threat.

topics.headline: protection echoes across corpus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears wider protection language behind the scene, while the local form does not become a divine-protection formula by itself (3:101, 5:67, 11:43).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite protection passages but the local grammar remains Joseph’s Form X action.

topics.headline: closed resistance texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the heavy consonants make the resistance feel closed and firm.
topics.reason: The phonetic row notes the emphatic consonant and final closure.

topics.headline: rare perfect protection verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pivot verb as distributionally marked, not ordinary narrative filler.
topics.reason: The rarity rows mark the perfect ʿ-ṣ-m form as exceptional.

topics.headline: Form X, protection, and pivot converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees form, root image, and position combine to make resistance the decisive pivot.
topics.reason: The convergence row synthesizes Form X, protection root, and pivot position.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the oath-conditional threat after confession and resistance
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new stage: after accusation, confession, and resistance, the wife moves into threat. The conjunction keeps the threat connected while preventing it from collapsing into the confession itself.

topics.headline: fresh stage into threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speech escalating into a distinct conditional threat unit.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the conditional threat clause after the resistance pivot.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lam preparing the oath-conditional threat architecture
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) begins the oath-conditional pressure before the conditional particle. It makes the coming if-not frame part of a heightened threat, not a casual condition.

topics.headline: oath-lam before conditional threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the condition already loaded with sworn intensity before the if-particle arrives.
topics.reason: The lam opens the wa-la-in conditional architecture and anticipates the emphatic apodosis.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle setting the if-not compliance test
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) supplies the threat’s logic: if he does not do what she commands, consequences will follow. The particle organizes the command as a compliance test with a double punishment attached.

topics.headline: conditional frame for compliance test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees coercion structured as if-not-then logic rather than a simple prediction.
topics.reason: The conditional particle governs the protasis linked to the double apodosis.

words.gloss_range: jussive negator making non-compliance the trigger
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) negates and governs the following jussive verb, defining the trigger as failure to comply. The threat turns not-doing into the condition for prison and humiliation.

topics.headline: negative jussive trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is tied to non-compliance, not to any named crime.
topics.reason: The jussive particle negates the following verb and shapes the protasis.

words.gloss_range: generic jussive doing under negation, with command content left deliberately open
words.root_gloss_range: doing, acting, making, and carrying out; locally narrowed to generic compliance with an open command.
words.prose: {{ar:يَفْعَلْ}} ({{tr:yafʿal}}) is a deliberately general action verb under jussive negation. It does not name the act demanded; it makes obedience itself the issue by taking the open command clause as its object. The condition moves from negation into that open object clause, and the same general doing language later participates in promise and moral-accounting scenes (12:61, 12:89).

topics.headline: jussive dependent verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verb grammatically subordinated to the negated condition.
topics.reason: The apocopated jussive form is controlled by the preceding negator.

topics.headline: generic doing as compliance test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the demanded act left unspecified so the condition centers on obedience to her command.
topics.reason: The broad f-ʿ-l root and object clause select general doing.

topics.headline: verbal core of protasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the condition from negation into an open object clause.
topics.reason: The verb is the core of the conditional protasis.

topics.headline: doing language across promises and reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this generic doing to later action and accountability language in the surah (12:61, 12:89).
topics.reason: The rows cite same-surah f-ʿ-l uses in promise and moral accounting scenes.

words.gloss_range: relative object pronoun opening the unspecified content of the command
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is relative here, not a negator. It carries the open object of doing: whatever she commands him, with the content left unspecified and therefore maximally coercive.

topics.headline: open relative object of compliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command’s content remains open while obedience becomes absolute.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun functions as the object of the doing verb and introduces the command clause.

words.gloss_range: present first-person command over Joseph, shifting from seduction to direct coercive authority
words.root_gloss_range: command, affair, order, decree, and authority; locally narrowed to a human command imposed on Joseph, with broader divine-command resonance only as contrast.
words.prose: {{ar:آمُرُهُ}} ({{tr:āmuruhū}}) shifts the wife’s strategy from coaxing to direct command: I command him. The present imperfect keeps the order active, the suffix makes Joseph its recipient, and the broader command/decree field is narrowed here to a human coercive claim that stands in tension with God’s command in the story (12:21, 12:68).

topics.headline: present first-person command with object suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command as current, personal, and aimed directly at Joseph.
topics.reason: The imperfect 1sg verb with 3ms object suffix encodes ongoing command.

topics.headline: human command against broader amr field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears authority and command pressure, while local grammar blocks turning this into counsel or prosperity.
topics.reason: The selected sense is command; alternate counsel or prosperity branches are not the local reading.

topics.headline: strategy shift from coaxing to command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rhetoric harden from seduction to direct authority.
topics.reason: The command clause supplies the object of generic doing after the earlier seduction verb.

topics.headline: human command contrasted with divine command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses the wife’s command as a human claim over against God’s command in the story (12:21, 12:68).
topics.reason: The rows cite same-surah and cross-surah amr contrasts, but local grammar remains her human command.

topics.headline: morphology and escalation converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees form, command semantics, and escalation all pointing to coercive control.
topics.reason: The convergence row synthesizes the local morphology and scene movement.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lam launching the first threatened apodosis
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) begins the first answer to the condition. Attached to the prison verb, it makes imprisonment a sworn and emphatic consequence rather than a vague possibility.

topics.headline: first apodosis emphatic lam
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the threat’s first consequence arrive with oath-response force.
topics.reason: The lam introduces the first apodosis verb and stacks with the emphatic ending.

words.gloss_range: passive emphatic future imprisonment threat, suppressing the jailer while certifying confinement
words.root_gloss_range: prison, confinement, and removal from circulation; locally a passive emphatic future imprisonment threat.
words.prose: {{ar:يُسْجَنَنَّ}} ({{tr:yusjananna}}) threatens Joseph with imprisonment in passive voice: the agent of confinement disappears, while the emphatic future form makes the outcome sound certain. The heavy nūn gives that certainty audible thickness, and the rare prison verb marks the motif as it forms the first limb of a double threat: physical confinement paired with social abasement. The prison root gives the threat concrete removal from circulation, and the next ayah reverses the force when Joseph says prison is preferable (12:33).

topics.headline: passive emphatic future prison verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both agency suppression and heavy certainty in the threatened imprisonment.
topics.reason: The passive imperfect, oath lam, and heavy nūn stack future threat force.

topics.headline: confinement and removal from circulation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels prison as concrete social and physical removal, not only a generic punishment.
topics.reason: The s-j-n field locally selects confinement and dungeon-like punishment.

topics.headline: first limb of double threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees imprisonment paired with a second social-status punishment rather than standing alone.
topics.reason: The passive prison clause is the first apodosis and is coordinated with humiliation.

topics.headline: prison motif from threat to chosen refuge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the threat answered and transformed by Joseph’s next speech (12:25, 12:33, 12:36, 12:41, 12:42, 12:100).
topics.reason: The rows cite the prison threat in 12:25, Joseph’s answer in 12:33, and later prison scenes.

topics.headline: heavy nūn certainty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the emphatic ending thicken the certainty of imprisonment.
topics.reason: The sound row notes repeated n-sounds and heavy nūn.

topics.headline: rare passive prison verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prison verb as a marked motif word in the Joseph story.
topics.reason: The rarity row marks the passive prison form as motif-heavy.

topics.headline: suppressed agency and future reversal converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the wife’s coercive threat already positioned for reversal by Joseph’s later choice.
topics.reason: The convergence row joins passive agency suppression, emphatic certainty, and forward reversal.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction adding the second punishment to the first
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates a second punishment with the first. The threat is cumulative: not only confinement, but also a new status among the humiliated.

topics.headline: coordination of double punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment has two coordinated limbs rather than one consequence.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the second apodosis with the prison clause.

words.gloss_range: second emphatic lam paralleling the prison-threat lam
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) repeats the same emphatic pressure before the second threat verb. The parallel lam makes status humiliation sound as certain as imprisonment.

topics.headline: parallel lam for second threat limb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the two punishments grammatically equalized by repeated emphasis.
topics.reason: The second lam scopes over the becoming verb in parallel with the prison limb.

words.gloss_range: emphatic future becoming, assigning Joseph to a degraded class rather than imposing a physical action
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, occurring, and status/place associations; locally narrowed to becoming classed among a degraded group.
words.prose: {{ar:يَكُونًۭا}} ({{tr:yakūnā}}) shifts the threat from bodily confinement to status reclassification: he will become among a group. The being/becoming root is narrowed by the following class phrase, and the marked light-nūn or tanwīn form gives this second limb a different emphatic shape from the heavy prison verb; same-surah contrasts show becoming used for opposite moral trajectories (12:9, 12:85).

topics.headline: marked emphatic becoming form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second threat has its own emphatic grammar, distinct from the heavy prison ending.
topics.reason: The imperfect verb carries lam and a marked tanwīn/light-nūn issue in the local writing.

topics.headline: becoming as status entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the common being verb narrowed into entry into a degraded status class.
topics.reason: The k-w-n plus following class phrase selects becoming/classification rather than bare existence.

topics.headline: second limb lands on reclassification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the closing threat broaden from prison to identity and status.
topics.reason: This verb begins the coordinated second apodosis after the prison clause.

topics.headline: same construction across moral trajectories
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this threatened becoming to other k-w-n plus group formulas in the surah (12:9, 12:85).
topics.reason: The rows cite becoming righteous in 12:9 and grief-state wording in 12:85.

topics.headline: lighter emphatic ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a distinct acoustic pressure in the humiliation limb compared with the heavy prison ending.
topics.reason: The phonetic row notes the light-nūn/tanwīn contrast.

topics.headline: marked form and status formula converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spelling, construction, and closure jointly mark the second punishment as reclassification.

words.gloss_range: classifying preposition turning becoming into membership among the humiliated

strongest_changes: Resistance becomes directional embodied escape whose rearward trace survives as evidence.
The demonstration turns private desire into publicly replicated susceptibility and reverses the flow of blame.
Protection becomes a relation between active self-binding and repeated divine redirection rather than isolated willpower.
Prison reverses from threatened abasement into a chosen defense of inner freedom, then materializes as institutional containment despite visible signs.
summary.what_was_special: The focus holds several rival restraint and governance systems at once: self versus household property, chosen protection versus imposed enclosure, her command versus a larger affair, and public speech that can confess, judge, recruit, and lower. Split-root branches also preserve live but contained readings of speech as diminution, blame as gathering, solicitation as recurrence, and resistance as residue.
remaining_uncertainties: The property mechanism is abductive: prior purchase and household rank establish vulnerability, but the packet does not explicitly state that she grounds her command in ownership.
The spectacle clearly reverses blame, but whether it intentionally recruits the women into coercion or only demonstrates her susceptibility remains open.
The nested-command reading depends on treating repeated root language across 12:21 and 12:32 as an organizing contrast rather than coincidence.
The four outliers depend on form-distant or material branches and must remain exploratory rather than displacing the dominant morphological readings.

2. **Protective restraint is opposed by imposed abasement.** ع ص م B001 (restraining hold that protects), س ج ن B001 (confinement), and ص غ ر B002 (abasement) form a contest over who controls Yusuf’s body and status. `استعصم` reads as active self-binding to protection; prison is threatened as the institution that will bind him otherwise.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:35 actualized the prison threat, while 12:54 reversed intended abasement into trusted standing before the king.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Refusal as taking a protective hold.** `ع ص م:B001` is “a restraining hold that protects,” including refusing by holding back and taking refuge; `ع ص م:B002` supplies the concrete holdfast image. Her admission places his *istaʿṣama* between prior solicitation and a future prison/humiliation threat; 12:33-34 shows him request and receive diversion from their pressure. The packet supplies pressure, hold, threat, and aid; I infer that resistance persists by attachment to a stronger constraint. The verb reads as active maintained refusal, not effortless invulnerability.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:79 repeats refuge language while refusing an expedient substitute, confirming that protection is an active hold on moral boundaries across both sexual pressure and administrative pressure.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه تسمية العين نفسا، وإصابة المنظور بنفس، والنافس بمعنى العائن.
يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الدم، والنفس السائلة، وتسميته نفسا لأن فقد الدم يذهب بالنفس.
يدخل فيه النفاس ولادة المرأة، والنفساء، والمنفوس بمعنى المولود، واستعماله في الحيض حيث نص المصدر عليه.
يدخل فيه الشرب بنفس أو أنفاس، والنفس بمعنى الجرعة أو المستراح في الشرب.
يدخل فيه النفس أو النفسين من الدباغ، أي مقدار يسير يدبغ به الجلد مرة أو مرتين.
يدخل فيه تسمية الماء نفسا، والشراب ذو النفس إذا كان فيه سعة وري، ونقيضه الشراب غير ذي نفس.
يدخل فيه تنفس الصبح والنهار إذا تبلج أو امتد، وتنفس القوس إذا انشقت، وزيادة الماء أو الموج حين يخرجان أو ينتشران.
يدخل فيه النفيس والنفاسة والمنفس، والرغبة والمنافسة في الشيء، والضن أو الحسد به إذا كان لقيمته ورغبة النفس فيه.
يدخل فيه النفس بمعنى الروح والحياة، وكل إنسان نفس، وخروج النفس عند الموت، والنفس الحية التي بها حياة الجسد.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tutma ve engelleme çekirdeğini; kötülükten koruma, bir koruyucuya tutunarak sakınma, direnip kaçınma ve bir şeye bağlı kalma yönleriyle birlikte verir. Sunulan dal çerçevesi bu eylem ve ilişki örgüsünü doğru biçimde karşılar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın engelleme ve koruma çekirdeğini türemiş biçimlerdeki tutunma, sığınma ve direnme yönlerinden ayırır; belirli tamlamalara özgü anlamları bütün dala yaymaz.

concept_map.definition: Birini ya da bir şeyi kötülükten veya zarardan alıkoyarak korumak; türemiş kullanımlarda ise bir koruyucuya ya da dayanağa sıkıca tutunup onunla korunmak, sığınmak veya boyun eğmemektir. Bir şeye bağlı kalma ve yemeğin açlığı gidermesi, bu çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir zararın kişiye veya şeye ulaşmasını engelleyerek onu koruma ve elde tutma eylemidir.
Türemiş biçimlerde kişi bir koruyucuya veya dayanağa tutunur, ona sığınır ve böylece zarar ya da yanlış davranıştan sakınır.
Direnme, boyun eğmeme ve bir şeye sıkıca bağlı kalma, tutunarak engellenme yönünü öne çıkaran özel kullanımlardır.
Yemeğin kişiyi açlıktan koruması, engelleyici korumanın somut bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar tutma, engelleme ve korumada birleşir; türemiş kullanımlar bu çekirdeği bir koruyucuya tutunma, sığınma, direnme ve bağlı kalma yönlerine taşır.
